messages.content: Determine the winner in a Poker game with John having a Hand of 8♥, 10♥, J♥, Q♥, K♥ and Mike having 9♠, J♠, 10♠, Q♠, K♠.

function.name: card_games_poker_determine_winner
function.description: Determines the winner in a game of Poker based on the cards in each players' hands. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

hand1.description: The list of cards (as strings) in first player's hand. E.g ['10♠', 'J♠']

hand2.description: The list of cards (as strings) in second player's hand. E.g ['9♥', '10♥']

message.content:
**Winner:** Mike

**Explanation**

- **John’s hand:** 8♥ 10♥ J♥ Q♥ K♥ – a flush (all hearts).  
- **Mike’s hand:** 9♠ 10♠ J♠ Q♠ K♠ – a flush (all spades).

Both are flushes, so we compare the highest cards:

| Rank | John | Mike |
|------|------|------|
| K    | ✔    | ✔    |
| Q    | ✔    | ✔    |
| J    | ✔    | ✔    |
| 10   | ✔    | ✔    |
| 9/8  | 8    | 9    |

Mike’s 9 is higher than John’s 8, so Mike wins the hand.
message.reasoning: We need to determine winner. John has 8♥,10♥,J♥,Q♥,K♥. That's a straight flush from 8 to K? Actually 8-10-J-Q-K is a straight flush (8-9-10-J-Q-K? Wait missing 9). Straight flush requires consecutive ranks. John's cards: 8,10,J,Q,K. Missing 9. So not straight flush. It's a flush (all hearts). Highest card K. Mike has 9♠, J♠,10♠,Q♠,K♠. That's also a flush (spades). Highest card K. But Mike has 9,10,J,Q,K. John's has 8,10,J,Q,K. Compare high cards: both have K. Next compare next highest: J vs J equal. Next Q vs Q equal. Next 10 vs 10 equal. Next 8 vs 9: Mike has 9, John has 8. So Mike wins. So answer: Mike wins.
